mainTopic: How drawn water (מים שאובין) disqualifies a מקוה "according to calculation" (לפי חשבון). The גמרא first reads this as the view of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, rejects that reading, and then רבה explains it as counting vessels, following יוסף בן חוני.
overview: The amud explains three lines of the משנה. First, drawn water disqualifies a מקוה 'according to calculation'. The גמרא first reads this as majority plus flowing, following רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, but that reading would leave רבי יוחנן's ruling (reported by רבין) with no תנא behind it. So רבה explains that 'calculation' means counting the vessels the water came from, following יוסף בן חוני, and a ברייתא shows his view. Next, the משנה says מי חטאת are made only by putting the ashes onto the water. רבי יוחנן says this is not like רבי שמעון, who uses a גזירה שוה on the word 'עפר' to link פרה and סוטה and allows either order. The גמרא then gives the תנא of our משנה's reading of the פסוק: the item that makes the water usable always goes on top. Finally, the משנה says one בית הפרס does not create another, which goes against רבי אליעזר. The amud ends by asking how far a בית הפרס reaches according to רבנן, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Drawn water becomes pure through majority and flowing
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the earlier explanation: the water in the מקוה is pure because drawn water is made kosher by a majority of good water and by flowing in.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all the water is pure, because drawn water is purified by a majority of good water and by flowing in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation that started before this section. It says drawn water does not ruin the מקוה when it flows in on top of a majority of kosher water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things work together here: רביה (most of the water is already kosher) and המשכה (the drawn water flows in rather than being poured straight in). Together they keep the מקוה kosher. That is how 'according to calculation' is being read at this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Drawn water: water that passed through a vessel, which can disqualify a מקוה
Here: a majority of kosher water already in the מקוה
Flowing: the water runs in along the ground instead of being poured directly

phrases.english: and they are pure,
phrases.notes: "They" means all the water in the מקוה, including the drawn water that flowed in.

phrases.english: since drawn water becomes purified
by a majority and by flowing.
phrases.notes: Majority means most of the water was already kosher. Flowing means the drawn water ran in rather than being dumped straight in.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵן טְהוֹרִין, שֶׁהַשְּׁאִיבָה מְטַהֶרֶת בִּרְבִיָּיה וּבְהַמְשָׁכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier explanation, which follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drawn water is made kosher by a majority of kosher water plus flowing in.

steps.title: Do רבנן reject majority and flowing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference: if this is only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view, then רבנן must hold that majority and flowing do not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean רבנן hold that a majority and flowing do not make it kosher?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the last step. This sets up the next step, where that conclusion will cause a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule of majority plus flowing belongs only to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, then רבנן must disagree. They would hold that drawn water disqualifies the מקוה even when it flows in. The next step shows why this is hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference: what follows from what was said

phrases.english: By inference, the Rabbis hold
that by majority and by flowing it does not [become kosher]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what step 1 means for רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do רבנן really hold that majority and flowing do not help?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's ruling would fit nobody
steps.stepSummary: רבין reported that רבי יוחנן said a מקוה made entirely of drawn water that flowed in is kosher. With the current reading, that ruling matches neither רבנן nor רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what about what רבין said when he came, in the name of רבי יוחנן: a מקוה made entirely of drawn water that was made to flow in is pure. Whose view is that? Not רבנן and not רבי אליעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 1. It shows that this reading leaves רבי יוחנן's ruling with no תנא behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says flowing alone is enough, even with no kosher majority at all. On the current reading, רבנן say flowing does not help, and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב needs a majority as well as flowing. So nobody holds like רבי יוחנן, and the reading must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A מקוה made of drawn water

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's case has no kosher water at all. It is all drawn water, and flowing alone makes it kosher. That is why it goes further than רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

phrases.english: But that which, when Ravin came,
Rabbi Yochanan said:
A mikveh entirely of drawn water that was made to flow in is pure.
Whose opinion is it?
Not the Rabbis, and not Rabbi Eliezer!
phrases.notes: "רבי אליעזר" here is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב from the earlier explanation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּכִי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 2 to show a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'according to calculation' means majority plus flowing, following רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading leaves רבי יוחנן's ruling (flowing alone makes even all-drawn water kosher) with no matching תנא.

steps.title: רבה: calculation means counting vessels
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives a new reading. 'According to calculation' means counting how many vessels the drawn water came from, and this follows יוסף בן חוני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: it means according to the count of vessels, and it is the view of יוסף בן חוני.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה drops the earlier reading and explains the משנה in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'calculation' is no longer about majority and flowing. It is about how many vessels poured the drawn water in. This frees רבי יוחנן's ruling from the problem in step 3.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:
according to the count of vessels,
and it is the view of Yosef ben Choni.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה: לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן כֵּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by replacing the earlier reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of the משנה, following a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Calculation' meant majority plus flowing, following רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Calculation' means the number of vessels, following יוסף בן חוני.

steps.title: The ברייתא of יוסף בן חוני
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the תנא קמא says three לוגין of drawn water disqualify the מקוה whether they came from 2–3 vessels or even 4–5. יוסף בן חוני says only 2–3 vessels disqualify, and 4–5 do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: three לוגין of drawn water that fell into the water, from two or three vessels, and even from four or five vessels, disqualify the מקוה. יוסף בן חוני says: from two or three vessels they disqualify the מקוה; from four or five they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source for רבה's reading. It shows that יוסף בן חוני makes the law depend on the number of vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, the number of vessels does not matter: three לוגין always disqualify. For יוסף בן חוני, if the three לוגין came spread over four or five vessels, they do not disqualify. That is the 'count of vessels' רבה meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Three לוגין: the amount of drawn water that disqualifies a מקוה

steps.whatToRemember: 'According to calculation' in the משנה means counting vessels, following יוסף בן חוני. Three לוגין from 2–3 vessels disqualify the מקוה; from 4–5 vessels they do not.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
Three log of drawn water
that fell into the water,
from two or three vessels,
and even from four or five vessels,
they invalidate the mikveh.
Yosef ben Choni says:
from two or three vessels
they invalidate the mikveh,
phrases.notes: Some versions have פוסל, in round brackets; the corrected wording is פוסלין, in square brackets. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: from four or five,
they do not invalidate the mikveh.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: שְׁלֹשֶׁת לוּגִּין מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לַמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for יוסף בן חוני's view that רבה relied on.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's reading that 'calculation' means counting vessels.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with the disagreement between the תנא קמא and יוסף בן חוני.

steps.title: Who taught the rule about making מי חטאת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that putting water onto the ashes does not make מי חטאת, and asks which תנא holds this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And water of purification is not made into water of purification, etc.' Which תנא taught this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about מי חטאת and asks whose view it is. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה holds that the ashes of the פרה אדומה must go onto the water, not the water onto the ashes. The גמרא wants to know if every תנא agrees, or if someone disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: Water of purification: spring water mixed with the ashes of the פרה אדומה
Who is the תנא? A question asking whose view a teaching follows

phrases.english: And water of purification does not
become water of purification, etc.
phrases.notes: Some versions say נעשה (singular) and the corrected wording is נעשין (plural); the meaning is the same. The משנה means: unless the ashes are put onto the water.

phrases.english: Who is the תנא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the מקוה discussion and returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the ashes must go onto the water for מי חטאת to be made.

steps.title: This rule does not follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא, quoting רבי יוחנן, answers that the משנה's rule is not like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it is not like רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the משנה does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tells us that רבי שמעון disagrees. He must hold that the order does not matter after the fact. The next step brings the source showing this.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in agreement with (a certain sage's view)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows the רבנן, not רבי שמעון.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון accepts dust put in before the water
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the dust was put in before the water, it is פסול, but רבי שמעון says it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If he put the dust in before the water, it is unfit. But רבי שמעון says it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי שמעון disagrees about the order of dust and water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא is about the dust put into the water of a סוטה, not about the פרה אדומה. The תנא קמא says the order is required, but רבי שמעון accepts the dust going in first. The גמרא will now show why this view carries over to מי חטאת too.

keyTerms.meaning: He put the dust in before the water
A woman suspected of being unfaithful, who drinks special water with dust from the משכן floor

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is about סוטה water, not מי חטאת. The link between the two cases only comes later, through the גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: As it is taught: If he put the dust in before the water, it is unfit,
phrases.notes: This is about the water given to a סוטה, where the כהן puts dust from the משכן floor into water (במדבר 5:17).

phrases.english: but Rabbi Shimon deems it fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי שמעון disagrees.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון disagrees with the order required by the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the סוטה water where רבי שמעון accepts dust placed before water.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבי שמעון's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון accepts dust put in first. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about סוטה seems to say water first, then dust. So the גמרא wants to know how רבי שמעון can allow the reverse order.

phrases.english: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי שמעון's view from step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the verses for רבי שמעון accepting dust placed before water.

steps.title: The פרה verse calls the ashes 'dust'
steps.stepSummary: The verse about the פרה אדומה says 'dust' of the burning, and רבי שמעון points out that it is really ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And for the impure they shall take of the dust of the burning of the purification, and put flowing water on it.' And a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says: Is it dust? It is ashes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by quoting the פרה אדומה verse and רבי שמעון's question about its odd word choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ashes of the פרה are אפר, yet the verse calls them עפר (dust). רבי שמעון takes this unusual word as a clue. The verse also says 'put water on it', which fits putting the ashes in first.

keyTerms.meaning: The burning of the sin-offering, meaning the burned פרה אדומה

phrases.english: As it is written: “And for the impure they shall take
of the dust of the burning of the purification offering,
and he shall put flowing water on it,”
and it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
But is it dust?
Isn't it ashes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פרה verse unusually calls ashes 'dust', which sets up a link to the סוטה verse.

steps.title: The גזירה שוה links פרה and סוטה
steps.stepSummary: The verse changed its normal wording to create a גזירה שוה on the word 'dust'. So the rules of סוטה and פרה are shared both ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse changed from its normal meaning to teach a גזירה שוה. 'Dust' is said here, and 'dust' is said there. Just as there, the dust goes on top of the water, so too here the dust goes on top of the water. And just as here, if the dust was put in before the water it is fit, so too there, if the dust was put in before the water it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי שמעון's reasoning: the shared word 'dust' teaches that both cases follow the same rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From סוטה, the פרה learns that the ashes should go on top of the water. From the פרה verse ('put water on it'), the סוטה learns that dust put in first is still fit. That is why רבי שמעון accepts both orders after the fact, unlike our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching that links two cases because the תורה uses the same word in both
The verse changed from its normal wording

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון links פרה and סוטה through the word 'עפר'. Both should have dust on top of the water, but in both, dust put in first is still כשר after the fact. Our משנה, which says water onto ashes does not work, is not like רבי שמעון.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a strange word in a verse can be a deliberate signal for a גזירה שוה, and how the link can teach rules in both directions.

phrases.english: The verse changed from its normal meaning
in order to learn a גזירה שוה from it:
“Dust” is said here,
and “dust” is said there.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן — עָפָר עַל גַּבֵּי הַמַּיִם,
phrases.english: Just as there, the dust is on top of the water,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן — עָפָר עַל גַּבֵּי הַמַּיִם.
phrases.english: so too here, the dust is on top of the water.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה כָּאן הִקְדִּים עָפָר לַמַּיִם — כָּשֵׁר,
phrases.english: And just as here, if he put the dust in before the water, it is fit,
phrases.notes: Now the direction flips: 'here' is the פרה, where the verse says to put water on the ashes.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן הִקְדִּים עָפָר לַמַּיִם — כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: so too here, if he put the dust in before the water, it is fit.
phrases.notes: This second 'here' means the סוטה case.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁינָּה הַכָּתוּב מִמַּשְׁמָעוֹ, לָדוּן הֵימֶנּוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי שמעון's reasoning begun in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Through a two-way גזירה שוה on 'עפר', רבי שמעון holds that dust should go on top of the water, but dust put in first is still כשר in both סוטה and פרה. The משנה disagrees with him.

steps.title: Where do we learn this for the פרה אדומה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that, for the פרה אדומה, the order of ashes and water does not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, by the פרה אדומה, how do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי שמעון learns that for the פרה אדומה you may put in the ashes or the water first. This sets up the next step, which brings the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the rules of סוטה and פרה are shared through the גזירה שוה. But that only works if the פרה itself already has this rule. So the גמרא wants to know where the פרה gets the rule from in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it? (asking for a source)
The red heifer, whose ashes are mixed with water to purify people from טומאת מת

phrases.english: And here, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: "Here" means the פרה אדומה: where does it get the rule that either order is fine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 11 said פרה and סוטה share their rules. Now the גמרא asks where the פרה's own rule comes from.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows the ashes of the פרה may go in before or after the water.

steps.title: Two parts of the verse point both ways, so either order works
steps.stepSummary: One phrase in the פסוק suggests the ashes go first, and another suggests the water goes first. So both orders are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two phrases are written. It says 'and put on it', which shows the ashes come first. Then it says 'running water into a vessel', which shows the water comes first. How do we fit them together? If he wants, the dust goes below. If he wants, the dust goes above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק contains two phrases that seem to clash about the order. It settles the clash by saying either order is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ונתן עליו' means putting water on top of the ashes, so the ashes are in first. 'מים חיים אל כלי' means water going into an empty vessel, so the water is in first. Since the פסוק supports both, the person may choose.

phrases.english: Two phrases are written:
phrases.notes: Both phrases come from the same פסוק, במדבר 19:17.

phrases.english: "And he shall put on it",
which shows the ashes come first,
and then it is written
"running water into a vessel."
How can this be?
If he wants, the dust goes below;
if he wants, the dust goes above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק has one phrase pointing to ashes first and one pointing to water first. So either order is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is רבי שמעון's source. Through the גזירה שוה, it also explains why he allows the dust first by סוטה.

steps.title: What is the reason of our משנה's תנא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the תנא of our משנה, who requires water first, deals with the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the other side and asks for the reasoning of the תנא of our משנה. He says that if the dust goes in first, it is פסול. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 showed that the פסוק seems to allow both orders. So the גמרא has to explain how our תנא can still require water first.

phrases.english: And our תנא, what is his reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving רבי שמעון's source, the גמרא asks how the other view reads the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the תנא of the משנה reads the פסוק so that it requires water first.

steps.title: The end of the verse is exact, and 'put on it' means to mix
steps.stepSummary: Our תנא says the end of the פסוק, 'running water into a vessel', is meant exactly. 'And put on it' only teaches that you must mix.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: the end of the verse is exact. 'And put on it' means to mix them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that our תנא treats the phrase about water going into the vessel as the real rule. He reads the other phrase as teaching something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For our תנא, water must go into the vessel first. The words 'ונתן עליו' do not teach the order at all. They only teach that the ashes and water must be mixed together.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of the פסוק

phrases.english: He would tell you:
the end of the verse is exact,
"and he shall put on it" means to mix them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The end of the פסוק sets the order (water first). 'ונתן עליו' teaches that the two must be mixed.

steps.title: Why not say the beginning of the verse is the exact part?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges our תנא: why choose the end of the פסוק as exact rather than the beginning?
steps.simpleTranslation: What did you see that made you say the end of the verse is exact? Maybe the beginning is exact!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 15. Choosing the end of the פסוק over the beginning looks random.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You could just as easily flip it. Then the beginning ('put on it') would set the order with ashes first, and the end would be explained some other way. The challenge asks for a real reason to prefer one side.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? (Why choose this side over the other?)

phrases.english: What did you see that made you say
the end of the verse is exact?
Perhaps the beginning is exact!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי חָזֵית דְּאָמְרַתְּ סֵיפֵיהּ דִּקְרָא דַּוְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading given in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our תנא's choice to treat the end of the פסוק as the exact part.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the פסוק itself makes the end more exact than the beginning. So the choice seems random.

steps.title: The item that makes the water usable always goes on top
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that everywhere, the item that makes the water usable goes on top. So here too, the ashes go on top of the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot say that. Just as we find everywhere that the item that makes it usable goes above, so too here the item that makes it usable goes above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends our תנא with a general pattern. The thing that makes the water work is always placed on top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By סוטה, the dust is put on top of the water. In the same way, the ashes of the פרה make the water usable, so they belong on top. That is why the end of the פסוק (water first) is the exact one.

keyTerms.meaning: The item that makes something usable (here, the ashes or dust)

steps.whatToRemember: For our תנא, water goes in first and the ashes go on top, because the item that makes the water usable always goes above.

phrases.english: You cannot say that,
since just as we find everywhere
the item that makes it usable goes above,
so too here, the item that makes it usable goes above.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ, מָה מָצִינוּ בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general pattern decides which part of the פסוק is exact.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either part of the פסוק could be the exact one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the item that makes the water usable always goes on top, the end of the פסוק (water first) is exact.

steps.title: Our משנה's בית הפרס rule is not like רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, that one בית הפרס does not create another. It says this does not follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And a בית הפרס does not make another בית הפרס, etc.' Our משנה is not like רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. It notes that this line goes against רבי אליעזר's opinion. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית הפרס is a field that is impure because a grave in it was plowed up. Our משנה says plowing from such a field into another field does not make the second field a בית הפרס too. The גמרא tells us whose opinion this is not.

keyTerms.meaning: A field that is impure because a grave in it was plowed up

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין בֵּית הַפְּרָס עוֹשֶׂה בֵּית הַפְּרָס כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: "And a בית הפרס does not make a בית הפרס, etc."
Our משנה is not like רבי אליעזר,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין בֵּית הַפְּרָס עוֹשֶׂה בֵּית הַפְּרָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of ashes and water and opens a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה's rule that one בית הפרס does not create another goes against רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Proof: רבי אליעזר says one בית הפרס does create another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה in which רבי אליעזר says one בית הפרס does create another.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי אליעזר says a בית הפרס makes another בית הפרס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves step 18 by quoting רבי אליעזר's opinion from another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that if you plow from a בית הפרס into another field, that field also becomes a בית הפרס. Our משנה says the opposite, so it cannot follow him.
steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה says one בית הפרס does not create another. רבי אליעזר disagrees.

phrases.english: as we learned: רבי אליעזר says:
a בית הפרס makes a בית הפרס.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in אהלות where רבי אליעזר says one בית הפרס creates another.

steps.title: How far does a בית הפרס reach according to the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far a בית הפרס extends according to the רבנן, and starts to bring the answer from רב דימי in the name of ריש לקיש and רבי שמעון בר אבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the רבנן, how far does it go? When רב דימי came, he said that ריש לקיש said that רבי שמעון בר אבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the size limit of a בית הפרס according to the רבנן. It then starts to introduce the answer, and the answer itself comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that one בית הפרס can create another, so the area keeps spreading. The רבנן say it does not spread, so the גמרא needs to know the exact edge of the area. The chain of names at the end is setting up the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the group who disagree with רבי אליעזר here
How far? Up to what distance?
A field that has the טומאה of a grave that was plowed over

phrases.english: And according to the Rabbis, how far?
When Rav Dimi came
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to בבל and brought teachings with him.

phrases.english: he said that Reish Lakish said
that Rabbi Shimon bar Abba said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing that רבי אליעזר lets a בית הפרס spread, the גמרא asks for the limit according to the רבנן, who do not let it spread.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact distance a בית הפרס extends according to the רבנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer begins with the chain of names רב דימי, ריש לקיש, and רבי שמעון בר אבא. Its content comes next.
